title: CJP finds in AAP an all-weather friend supporting it at every turn
author: Nikhil M Babu
content_html:
Within hours of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka posting a video on X on August 21 about him and other CJP volunteers being attacked while checking the quality of government schools in Rajasthan, another X user — AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal — quote-retweeted it, blaming the BJP for the attack.

“What’s going on in the country? BJP’s goons have brutally attacked CJP’s volunteers. They beat them up, tore their clothes, and smashed the car windows. Is all this just so they can’t raise their voices for giving kids a good education?” Mr. Kejriwal said in a post on X on August 21, retweeting Mr. Ranka’s post.

The retweet gathered more likes and reposts than the original post, and it is not a lone case.

Since the beginning of the CJP, Mr Kejriwal, other top leaders, and the AAP ecosystem have supported it, even before it became a mass movement in Delhi, drawing tens of thousands of people to Jantar Mantar every day.

On August 18, when right-wing handles were attacking CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleging that his degree was fake, Mr. Kejriwal retweeted a video on Mr. Dipke, extending his support.

On August 17, when the Rajasthan Government restricted entry of outsiders into government schools, following a CJP campaign to check government schools, Mr. Kejriwal said in a post on X, “Instead of banning outsiders’ entry, why not fix the school?”

Even in the initial days of the CJP movement, Mr. Kejriwal supported it online and asked people to join the protest at Jantar Mantar. Later in July, he visited the protest site along with other leaders.

Both Mr. Dipke and Mr. Ranka have worked for the AAP in the past, while CJP co-convenor Saurav Das’s proximity to Mr. Kejriwal is hardly a secret.

Interestingly, the support by the larger AAP ecosystem has been more than merely extending political support at crucial junctures.

“15000 + GenZ crowd at Connaught Place right now because Jantar Mantar is packed . Naturally without any call of protest. #CJP” AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj said in a post on X on July 21. He has made several such posts supporting the CJP.

The X timeline of Akshay Marathe, who wrote articles as an “AAP spokesperson” until February last year, has over the last two months been filled with posts supporting the CJP.

“Abhijeet Dipke shares his story in this fantastic 10-minute film produced by the New York Times. The cockroaches paint India in the best light possible in these times. Watch this — it will make you proud of young Indians!” Mr. Marathe posted on X on Sunday.

“Power of a mass movement — everyone is spurred into action to protect their jobs! From politicians to bureaucrats,” Mr. Marathe said while retweeting a video posted on X by Mr. Dipke on how authorities have visited a school after CJP raised issues.

“Hum Jeet Gayeeeeeeeeeee,” Mr. Marathe said on Facebook on July 25 when Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister, while he posted a video about Mr. Dipke and the movement.

title: FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi over Haldwani 'purification' remarks
author: PTI
content_html:
An FIR has been registered against Rahul Gandhi, following a complaint by a member of the Valmiki community in Haldwani alleging that the Congress leader gave a casteist spin to a religious ritual held at the venue of the AICC chief's programme, police said on Sunday (August 30, 2026).

The FIR has been registered under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) concerning the promotion of enmity between groups and deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings. The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, has also been invoked, police said.

Amit Kumar, a resident of Jawahar Nagar and a Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas member, claimed in the complaint filed at the Haldwani police station that he was present during the "ritual and cleanliness drive" and Mr. Gandhi's remarks made in Delhi at a press conference on August 29 hurt the sentiments of the community.

He accused Mr. Gandhi of portraying those associated with the ritual as practising "untouchability" and being "anti-Dalit".

In the complaint, Mr. Kumar claimed that he belongs to the Scheduled Caste community and that people from different sections of society, including Scheduled Castes, were involved in the ritual, which, according to him, had "no connection" with Congress president Mallkarjun Kharge's caste.

A political row erupted after some individuals allegedly performed a 'purification yajna' at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani on August 11, following a public meeting held there by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge on August 8.

While the Congress has termed the incident a reflection of the BJP's anti-Dalit mindset, the BJP defended the action, claiming that the venue was left littered after Mr. Kharge's rally and that slogans were raised which were inappropriate for a religious site.

At a press conference in New Delhi on August 29, Mr. Gandhi criticised the incident and demanded registration of an FIR under the SC/ST Act against those responsible for the "purification".

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra subsequently joined the demand for action, describing the incident as a reflection of a "reprehensible and shameful mindset" and alleging that it amounted to a violation of the SC/ST Act.

title: Maratha quota: Maharastra Govt hints at willingness to discuss ‘legally valid’ demands
author: PTI
content_html:
Walking the quota tightrope amid contrasting aspirations of Marathas and OBCs, the Maharashtra government on Sunday (August 30, 2026) indicated its willingness to discuss "legally valid" demands of the Maratha community even as fasting activist Manoj Jarange remained firm on the Kunbi caste certificate.

On the second day of his indefinite hunger strike launched from Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district, Mr. Jarange set a September 12 deadline for the government to accept his demands and warned of demonstrations by members of the Maratha community in Mumbai.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Jarange opposed a rally of Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, also a Maratha, in Parbhani city, questioning the need for the "political event". Police detained some individuals, an official said, without elaborating.

Reacting cautiously, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the government is open to discussing constitutionally valid and legally viable demands, and not those violative of the Supreme Court's orders.

Addressing the rally of agriculturists, Mr. Shinde said the Mahayuti government and Mr. Jarange are on the same page in supporting farmers, highlighting the state's commitment to do justice to the community.

He rejected allegations that the rally was aimed at political muscle flexing.

Speaking to reporters in Nagpur, Mr. Fadnavis said the government’s representatives are attending the Parbhani event to discuss the demands of (Maratha) protesters.

"Earlier also we found a way to address their issues, and we are going forward to resolve their demands. Similarly, Eknath Shinde is also very sensitive to these issues from the very beginning," he said.

Jarange has claimed that 58 lakh records were found of the Kunbi genealogical link of Marathas and that the government was trying to slash this figure.

His principal demand is Kunbi recognition for members of the Maratha community, similar to the benefits enjoyed by OBC groups in education and government jobs.

The other demands include the reservation based on the Satara Gazette, withdrawal of all police cases registered against quota protesters across Maharashtra, and providing government jobs and financial compensation to the families of those who died during the previous agitations.

title: Report lists persistent hotspots for elephant mortality and human casualties in Keralam
author: K.S. Sudhi
content_html:
Villages of Keralam, namely Kanan Devan Hills, Kuttampuzha, Chittar, Mankulam, Padavayal, and Peechi, have been identified as persistent hotspots for both elephant mortality and human casualties.

As many as 21 villages have also been classified as areas of high incidence of human-elephant conflicts (HEC), where 20 or more human casualties were reported.

The villages that are prone to HEC were listed in a recent report, ‘HEC in the State of Keralam 2008-2025, trends challenges and insights,’ released by the Wildlife Institute of India.

Of the 214 villages from where human mortality and injury incidents occurred during the study period, 175 were classified as low incidence (0-10 incidents), 18 as medium incidence (10-20 incidents), and 21 villages as high incidence (more than 20 incidents).

Most impacted division

Ranni was identified as the most impacted forest division with records of 169 HEC cases. Munnar division followed with 144 cases, while Munnar Wildlife and Nilambur North divisions each reported 138 and 108 cases respectively.

Although HEC affected many villages, the majority experienced relatively few incidents with only a small proportion of villages being identified as high-conflict hotspots, it noted.

Nilambur, Palakkad-Mannarkkad, Munnar-Mankulam, and Kothamangalam-Periyar landscapes have been identified as major hotspots of HEC, with a high concentration of incidents occurring in and around these forest divisions.

The highest number of human deaths was recorded in Nilambur South (78), followed by Palakkad (57), Mankulam (57), Munnar (50), Periyar East (42), Nilambur North division (27 cases). Kothamangalam accounted for the highest number of human injuries (164), followed by Marayoor (102), Nilambur North (63), Periyar East (64), and Thiruvananthapuram (58). The period also saw 1,781 incidents of HEC leading to 581 human deaths and 1,200 injuries in the State.

Elephant deaths

Electrocution was found to be the major anthropogenic factor contributing to elephant deaths as 154 elephants died after coming into contact with live wires. While explosive baits killed 12 elephants, retaliatory killing took the lives of 11 elephants. Poisoning (5), poaching (7) and snare/trap incidents (4) accounted for 16 deaths, according to researchers.

Solitary adult males were found responsible for the highest proportion of HEC incidents, especially raiding crop lands and causing damage to properties. Translocation of conflict elephants rarely provided a long-term solution, as many of them attempted to return to their original home ranges or continued to cause conflict in new areas after release, quoting a study from Sri Lanka, the report concluded.

A similar pattern was observed in Keralam during the translocation of the elephant Arikomban from Chinnakkanal in 2023, where it moved into human-dominated areas after release, requiring further management interventions. Repeated translocation of conflict elephants often provided only temporary relief, it was reported.
